text_post: Brace yourselves, this one is truly beyond the pale: http://www.npr.org/2014/09/29/352276...out-lost-girls Whew - what a doozy! How fucking deluded do you have to be, to think the phrase, 'Too much information' is sexist towards women?  I can recall many, many times - in my own life, and in films and TV shows that I've seen, where that phrase was directed from one man to another.  From my experience, that phrase is almost universally associated with a man being 'too comfortable' sharing very personal information, regarding his sex life, masturbation, other bodily functions, etc.  Either that, or someone (male or female) is being excessively long-winded, and not reading the social cues of people around them, who have long since lost interest in the topic.   But maybe that's the problem, Lena - maybe you're just boring as hell, in addition to being an industrial-strength narcissist.  So whenever YOU hear that phrase, it's merely a reference to your own social toxicity and innate dullness. Once again, please stop bringing ALL WOMEN into the discussion, in describing something that is entirely unique to YOU. But lets revisit another part of her quote: Okay, excuse me while I go finish my hysterical laughing fit.  You think men are perceived as BRAVE when they 'share their experiences'??  Have you ever actually TALKED to a man about any of this, to learn about HIS perspective?  Phrases like 'man up' and 'you're such a whiner' quickly come to mind, as common responses to men sharing their experiences - from both men AND women. Come to think of it, I seem to recall a particular social movement, comprised of a significant number of people who've struggled to share their experiences without being humiliated for doing it.  And then YOU went on national TV and slandered them as a bunch of desperate, angry, creepy losers. *** I think it's time we coin a new popular phrase, specifically for Lena. Instead of 'TMI', it would be 'TMB', or 'Too much BULLSHIT'.  How does that sound?
